title: bugbot findings
description: findings.json: what the review of one PR round found, assembled by `bugbot findings` from the finders' candidates (candidates/*.json) and the verifiers' verdicts (verdicts/**/*.json) into the PR's cache folder (path in meta.json paths.findings). Every candidate is here, kept and cut, with its verdicts. One file per round, replaced on the next round: the head sha says which. A missing file means the review did not run; `verdict` says what an empty list means.

findings.title: Clear button stays pressed after the field loses focus
findings.explanation: `clearPressedState` is reset only when `clearVisible` turns false. With `showClearButtonOnBlur`, the button stays visible after blur, so a press interrupted by the blur leaves it rendered as pressed until the next touch.

evidence.note: the only reset of the pressed state

evidence.quote: const clearVisible = filledState && resolvedEditable !== false && (focusState || showClearButtonOnBlur);
evidence.note: stays true on blur when showClearButtonOnBlur is set

verdicts.reason: Evidence matches the diff; no other reset of clearPressedState in the file.
Reproduced by reading the effect dependencies.

findings.title: New boolean prop has no story showing it enabled
findings.explanation: `hasPadding` is added to the public API, but no story renders it with `true`, so the visual regression suite never covers the padded state.

rule.quote: Every new public prop has a story that exercises it.

verdicts.reason: Rule quoted verbatim; no story sets hasPadding.
Stories were not part of the reviewed files.

findings.title: Layout handler re-renders the whole component on every frame
findings.explanation: `setContentWidth` runs on every layout event, which re-renders the component during the focus animation.

verdicts.reason: React skips the re-render when the rounded width is unchanged; layout events fire on size changes, not per frame.
Claim inferred from the handler name; no frame-rate evidence.

head.description: Head sha that was reviewed (meta.json head.sha). publish refuses a file whose head is not the PR's current head: findings of an older round would anchor on lines that moved.

depth.description: Depth the review ran at: the decision recorded in triage.json for this head.

verdict.description: REQUEST_CHANGES: at least one kept Critical or High that is not pre-existing. COMMENT: a kept Medium, or a kept pre-existing Critical/High. PASS: only kept Low findings or none; publish as APPROVE. SKIPPED: the review decided not to run (say why in `note`). INVALID_INVOCATION: the review could not run (missing input).

note.description: Required for SKIPPED and INVALID_INVOCATION: why.

round.description: Which review round this is and what it covered (triage.json round).

carried.description: Findings carried from the previous round without a new verification.

finders.description: Finders that ran, with the domains each covered: shows what was looked at, including the domains nothing ran on.

findings.description: Every finding raised this round, kept and cut. Report a kept finding again on every round even if an earlier round raised it: publish deduplicates by fingerprint, and a finding missing from a round is how it learns the problem may be gone.

id.description: Stable within this file: F1, F2... Verifier notes and the summary refer to findings by it.

domain.description: Domain of `file` as triage.json reports it (files[].domain). Decides which finder raised it.

finder.description: Name of the finder that raised it (for example bugs, security, convention). Free text, one name per finder.

severity.description: Finding severity: Critical, High, Medium or Low, as defined in .agents/shared/review-rules.md and refined by the repository's REVIEW.md.

pre_existing.description: The problem exists on the base branch too; the PR touched the code around it but did not introduce it. Reported as information, never as a reason to block.

category.description: What kind of problem: correctness, security, performance, api-contract, accessibility, convention, test, docs.

title.description: One line, the problem and not the fix, in the language of the review. Part of the fingerprint: keep it stable across rounds for the same problem.

explanation.description: Why it is a problem and what happens at runtime, in Markdown. Becomes the comment body.

suggestion.description: Optional replacement for the anchored line(s), exact code that compiles. Rendered as a GitHub suggestion block, so only when the fix fits the commented lines.

file.description: Path from the repository root, as in the diff.

line.description: Line on `side` the comment anchors to. Must be a line of the diff to become an inline comment; otherwise the finding goes to the review body under 'Outside the diff'.

side.description: RIGHT: the line in the PR's version (added or unchanged). LEFT: a removed line, in the base version.

evidence.description: What the finding rests on, checkable by someone else: the code quoted verbatim from the file, and the file:line of every other place the claim depends on (caller, rule, test). A claim inferred from a name is not evidence.

rule.description: The written rule a convention finding enforces: where it is (file and heading) and the sentence quoted. Required for category convention: without it the comment reads as taste.

source.description: File and section, e.g. REVIEW.md#Always check or AGENTS.md:42.

confidence.description: CONFIRMED: the evidence was read and holds. PLAUSIBLE: likely, but checking it would need running code or reading more than is cheap; rendered with a note.

carried_from.description: Head of the round this kept finding comes from, when it was carried over because the PR did not change its file since (round scope delta or unchanged). Absent when found this round.

verification.description: The verifiers' verdicts. A finding is published only when kept; cut findings stay in the file for the audit table and are never posted.

file.description: Path from the root of the repository the line is in: this PR's, or `repo`'s. Installed dependencies and repositories outside the workspace cannot be checked by a verifier, so they go in the explanation, not here.

repo.description: Another repository of the workspace (owner/name, a key of workspace.json repos) when the line is there, for example the code a documentation page describes. Read from its clone at its default branch: `git -C <path> show <remote>/<default_branch>:<file>`; `ref` does not apply. Omitted: this PR's repository.

ref.description: Version the line comes from: head (the PR, read in the worktree; default) or base (the merge base, for code the PR removed or changed: `git show <merge_base>:<file>`).

quote.description: Verbatim text of that line (or the few lines around it).

note.description: Why this line matters to the claim.

reason.description: One sentence; for cut, the concrete reason (evidence does not match the code, rule misquoted, outside the PR's change, duplicate of F<n>).

outcome.description: keep: published. cut: shown only in the audit table. Majority of verdicts; a tie or only unsure verdicts is cut with confidence PLAUSIBLE never upgraded.

duplicate_of.description: Id of the finding this one repeats; set when cut as duplicate.
